description:
The workspace 'hybrid sloppy-Value + opt-in typed sub-types' pattern (workspace AGENTS.md §Sloppy-Value) ships typed sub-object types via two re-export surfaces from the *-types crates:

- Top-level: `jmap_contacts_types::Name`, `jmap_contacts_types::EmailAddress`, etc. (30+ types from jmap-jscontact-types).
- Module alias: `jmap_contacts_types::jscontact::*` (entire upstream crate).
- Parallel surface in `jmap_calendars_types::jscalendar::*` (full upstream re-export).

The mechanism is correct and consistent with the workspace's canonical-template rule. The gap is that **the workspace has no documented stability contract for how these re-exports evolve**.

Concrete risks:
- If `jmap-jscontact-types::Name` is renamed to `JsContactName`, both surfaces in `jmap-contacts-types` break consumers downstream.
- If `jmap-jscontact-types` adds a non-default field to any of these types, match-arm exhaustiveness in downstream `match` statements breaks (#[non_exhaustive] handles struct-literal construction but not match destructure).
- If `jmap-jscontact-types` cuts a major version (0.x → 0.y) under semver, every downstream consumer of `jmap-contacts-types` has to coordinate the upgrade.

Decisions needed:
1. Should the re-export surface (top-level vs module alias vs both) be canonical workspace policy? Currently it is implicit precedent.
2. Should the *-types crate version-pin the re-exported crate at `=0.x.y` (tighter) or `^0.x` (looser)? Currently it's a path-dep so the question deferred to crates.io release time.
3. Should additions to upstream sub-types automatically propagate via the top-level re-export, or should *-types crates re-export individually per RFC version?

Recommendation: document the policy in workspace AGENTS.md as a successor to the Sloppy-Value section. Choose option (a) both surfaces (status quo), with version-pin at `=0.x.y` once the crates hit crates.io; and document that any breaking change in the re-exported sub-types-only crate is by definition a breaking change in the consuming *-types crate.

Trigger: JMAP-glx8.15 contacts-types review — same shape applies to calendars-types and the planned tasks-types JSCalendar re-exports (JMAP-yfpq).
title: Workspace policy: stability contract for hybrid type-crate re-exports (jscontact, jscalendar)
